ev.section: HarmBench: A Standardized Evaluation Framework for Automated Red Teaming and Robust Refusal
ev.quote: HarmBench: A Standardized Evaluation Framework for Automated Red Teaming and Robust Refusal

venue.value: ICML 2024 (Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning)

contribution.value: HarmBench is a standardized red-teaming benchmark with 510 harmful behaviors across 4 functional categories used to compare 18 attack methods on 33 LLMs, and the paper introduces R2D2, an efficient adversarial training defense.

ev.quote: we introduce HarmBench, a standardized evaluation framework for automated red teaming. We identify several desirable properties previously unaccounted for in red teaming evaluations and systematically design HarmBench to meet these criteria. Using HarmBench, we conduct a largescale comparison of 18 red teaming methods and 33 target LLMs

datasets.value: HarmBench (510 harmful behaviors: 400 textual + 110 multimodal; 100 validation / 410 test)

ev.quote: HarmBench contains 510 unique harmful behaviors, split into 400 textual behaviors and 110 multimodal behaviors
Standard behaviors are modeled after existing datasets of harmful behaviors, including AdvBench and the TDC 2023 Red Teaming Track dataset
Standard behaviors are modeled after existing datasets of harmful behaviors, including AdvBench and the TDC 2023 Red Teaming Track dataset (Zou et al., 2023; Mazeika et al., 2023)
we conduct a small-scale experiment on the searchability of HarmBench contextual behaviors compared to behaviors in two prior behavior datasets: MaliciousInstruct and Advbench

datasets.value: UltraChat (instruction-tuning dataset for R2D2 SFT loss)

ev.quote: We use UltraChat as the dataset for the SFT loss, building on the Zephyr codebase
we show the performance of Zephyr 7B + R2D2 on MT-Bench, an evaluation of general knowledge and conversational ability for LLMs

data_size.value: 510 harmful behaviors total: 200 standard + 100 copyright + 100 contextual + 110 multimodal; split into 100 validation and 410 test behaviors

ev.quote: HarmBench contains the following 4 functional categories of behavior: standard behaviors, copyright behaviors, contextual behaviors, and multimodal behaviors. These categories contain 200, 100, 100, and 110 behaviors, respectively
The primary measure of a red teaming method's success is its attack success rate (ASR) on a given target model, which is the percentage of test cases that elicit the behavior from the target model

eval_metrics.value: Classifier agreement rate vs. human judgment

ev.quote: Agreement rates between previous metrics and classifiers compared to human judgments on our manually labeled validation set
The MT-Bench scores of these models are 6.0 and 6.5, respectively

eval_metrics.value: Searchability rate (% of behaviors solvable via Google)

ev.quote: The searchability rate was 55% for MaliciousInstruct, 50% for AdvBench, and 0% for HarmBench contextual behaviors

key_results.value: Average ASR across 18 attacks shows AutoDAN highest (52.7%) and PAP-top5 lowest among automated attacks (16.6%); Direct Request baseline is 25.3%
Zephyr 7B + R2D2 cuts GCG ASR from 69.4% (vanilla Zephyr 7B) to 5.5%, beating Llama 2 7B Chat (31.8 -> 5.9) and Llama 2 13B Chat (30.2 -> 5.9)

ev.quote: Zephyr 7B + R2D2 obtains state-of-the-art robustness against GCG among model-level defenses, outperforming Llama 2 7B Chat (31.8 \rightarrow 5.9) and Llama 2 13B Chat (30.2 \rightarrow 5.9) in percent ASR

key_results.value: HarmBench classifier reaches 93.19% average agreement with human labels, exceeding GPT-4 (88.37%), GPTFuzz (75.42%), AdvBench substring (69.93%) and Llama-Guard (66.94%)

ev.quote: AdvBench | GPTFuzz | ChatGLM(Shen et al., 2023b) | Llama-Guard(Bhatt et al., 2023) | GPT-4(Chao et al., 2023) | HarmBench(Ours) | ... Average (↑) | 69.93 | 75.42 | 64.29 | 66.94 | 88.37 | 93.19

key_results.value: Robustness is independent of model size: no correlation between scale and ASR within the six tested model families spanning 7B to 70B parameters

ev.quote: we find no correlation between robustness and model size within model families in our results. This is illustrated in Figure 6 across six model families, four red teaming methods, and model sizes ranging from 7 to 70 billion parameters

key_results.value: On multimodal models, MultiModalPGD reaches up to 82.73% ASR (Qwen-VL-Chat), and Render Text attacks score much lower (1.82-20.00%)

ev.quote: we introduce HarmBench, a standardized evaluation framework for automated red teaming
we introduce HarmBench, a standardized evaluation framework for automated red teaming

hardware.value: NVIDIA A100 (8x A100 node for R2D2 training)

ev.quote: This takes 16 hours on an 8xA100 node

hardware.value: A100 (single GPU for GCG attack timing on 7B models)

ev.quote: GCG is extremely slow, requiring 20 minutes to generate a single test case on 7B parameter LLMs using an A100

strengths.value: First large-scale standardized red-teaming benchmark covering 18 attacks and 33 LLMs (open and closed), enabling cross-paper comparison.

ev.quote: Using HarmBench, we conduct a largescale comparison of 18 red teaming methods and 33 target LLMs and defenses, yielding novel insights

strengths.value: Introduces 4 functional categories (standard, copyright, contextual, multimodal) covering 510 behaviors with validation/test split.

ev.quote: HarmBench contains 510 unique harmful behaviors, split into 400 textual behaviors and 110 multimodal behaviors

strengths.value: Open-source Llama 2 13B fine-tuned classifier reaches 93.19% agreement with human labels, beating GPT-4 (88.37%) and prior open classifiers.

ev.quote: Our classifier, trained on distilled data from GPT-4-0613, achieves performance comparable to GPT-4

strengths.value: Open-source code release at github.com/centerforaisafety/HarmBench supports reproducibility and downstream evaluation work.

weaknesses.value: R2D2 generalises poorly to attacks dissimilar to its train-time GCG adversary, including PAIR, TAP, and Stochastic Few-Shot.

ev.quote: For some attacks, the improvement conferred by R2D2 is less pronounced. This is especially true for methods dissimilar to the train-time GCG adversary, including PAIR, TAP, and Stochastic Few-Shot

weaknesses.value: R2D2 modestly hurts utility: MT-Bench drops from 7.34 (Zephyr 7B) and 6.5 (Mistral 7B Instruct v0.2) to 6.0 for Zephyr 7B + R2D2.
Copyright behavior ASR is low across all models because the hashing classifier requires verbatim copyrighted text, not just attempted output.

ev.quote: On copyright behaviors, ASR is relatively low. This is because our hashing-based copyright classifier uses a stricter standard than our non-copyright classifiers, requiring that completions actually contain the copyrighted text to be labeled positive

weaknesses.value: No single attack or defense is uniformly effective; all attacks have low ASR on at least one LLM and all LLMs are weak against at least one attack.

ev.quote: no current attack or defense is uniformly effective. All attacks have low ASR on at least one LLM, and all LLMs have poor robustness against at least one attack

limitations.value: The paper does not test any quantized or compressed LLMs; all targets are full-precision (typically FP16) checkpoints.

ev.quote: We include 33 LLMs in our evaluation, consisting of 24 open-source LLMs and 9 closedsource LLMs

limitations.value: Only data-centre GPUs (A100) are used; no edge or mobile deployment scenarios are evaluated.

ev.quote: This takes 16 hours on an 8xA100 node

limitations.value: Energy consumption, real per-token latency, and throughput are not reported for any target model.
Long-context evaluation is absent; behaviors are short prompts and the framework standardises only N=512 generation tokens.

ev.quote: we standardize this parameter to N = 512 to allow the metric to converge

future_work_stated.value: Incorporate multiple diverse attacks into adversarial training to obtain generalisable robustness beyond GCG.

ev.quote: This suggests that incorporating multiple diverse attacks into adversarial training may be necessary to obtain generalizable robustness

future_work_stated.value: Use HarmBench to enable codevelopment of stronger attacks and defences across the community.

ev.quote: Ultimately, we hope HarmBench can enable collaborative development of stronger attacks and defenses

future_work_stated.value: Develop sophisticated multidimensional defences, since no model is robust to all evaluated attacks.

ev.quote: no model is robust against all malicious attacks we evaluate against, emphasizing the need for sophisticated, multidimensional defense strategies
